title: Mira L. Sedgewick v. Harborline Support Services, LLC
jurisdiction_basis: 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331, 1291; 29 U.S.C. §§ 207(a)(1), 216(b); final judgment disposing of sole federal claim; private represented parties.

timeline.description: Sedgewick begins hourly nonexempt customer support employment.
Supervisor sends team reminder about completion of assigned cases.
Plaintiff asks supervisor about closing time and time entry.
Last of four relevant payroll periods paid.
Payroll corrects separate previously submitted missed-punch request.
Order granting summary judgment and separate judgment entered.

issues.question: Whether the evidence, viewed for the nonmovant, permits a reasonable jury to find uncompensated overtime work and actual or constructive employer knowledge under the FLSA.
issues.standard_of_review: De novo; Rule 56 nonmovant reasonable inferences, substantive FLSA knowledge and worktime requirements.
issues.preservation_status: Raised in opposition and June 29 hearing; resolved in final summary judgment.
issues.appellant_theory: Specific after-punch user events and supervisor communications support inference of work and knowledge; correction process does not automatically defeat liability.
issues.appellee_theory: Event timestamps do not measure continuous work, general reminder and prompt direction to correct time do not establish employer knowledge of actual uncompensated work; no reliable weekly duration evidence.
issues.appellant_relief: Vacate summary judgment and remand for further proceedings.
issues.ruling_quote: Defendant's motion for summary judgment is granted.
issues.preservation_quote: The record permits a reasonable inference of work and employer knowledge.

brief_record_refs.quote: Defendant's motion for summary judgment is granted. The sole claim seeks overtime compensation under the Fair Labor Standards Act for four weeks ending May 26, 2024. The court considers the record cited by both parties and draws reasonable inferences in plaintiff's favor. The court does not make a finding that plaintiff's testimony was untruthful, that the application records were fabricated, or that a failure to request a payroll correction automatically bars recovery. The ruling concerns the sufficiency of the evidence on the elements of the particular claim.
brief_record_refs.review_status: Source page compared; cited factual proposition within source page.

brief_record_refs.quote: Pursuant to the order granting Defendant's motion for summary judgment entered this date, judgment is entered in favor of Harborline Support Services, LLC and against Mira L. Sedgewick on the sole claim for overtime compensation under the Fair Labor Standards Act. Plaintiff shall take nothing on the claim. This judgment resolves all claims between the parties. The Clerk is directed to close the district case. Any application for taxable costs or attorney fees shall be made separately in accordance with applicable rules. No determination of a specific amount of costs is made by this judgment.
brief_record_refs.review_status: Source page compared; cited factual proposition within source page.

brief_record_refs.quote: Under Tolan v. Cotton, 572 U.S. 650, 656–57 (2014) [[AUTH:TOL:P1]], the court must credit the nonmovant's evidence and draw justifiable inferences in her favor. Plaintiff's recollection of completing assigned notes may support an inference that some activity occurred after a punch. Yet the timestamps are not measurements of active work. The custodian explains that the server records accepted events and that composition, transmission and acceptance are distinct. IDEP 3–10, 16–20. Plaintiff does not recall a reliable duration and expressly disclaims equating the elapsed intervals with work. PDEP 8–13, 16, 22, 26. The coworker's general observations do not establish dates or punches. WDEP 4, 12. The court concludes that the proffered intervals lack a sufficient factual basis to infer the amount and extent of uncompensated work in each particular week.
brief_record_refs.review_status: Source page compared; cited factual proposition within source page.

brief_record_refs.quote: The court concludes the evidence is insufficient to create a genuine issue on the amount and extent of compensable work beyond forty hours and, independently, on actual or constructive knowledge of the alleged unpaid overtime. The ruling extends to the final disputed date after the exchange because plaintiff supplied no new information identifying actual missed work and the evidence does not establish contemporaneous observation of that event. The court has not fixed the amount of damages or determined the truth of disputed witness recollections. Judgment shall be entered for defendant on the sole claim. The separate judgment will resolve the action. Any collateral matter not decided here is governed by applicable procedure.
